definitions.gloss: funeral hall; funeral parlor; funeral home
definitions.explanation: A facility where funeral services and ceremonies are held. May include spaces for the wake, the funeral ceremony, and sometimes cremation.

examples.japanese: {葬儀場|そうぎじょう}の{場所|ばしょ}を{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I confirmed the location of the funeral hall.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}から{葬儀場|そうぎじょう}までバスが{出|で}ている。
examples.english: There is a bus running from the station to the funeral hall.

examples.japanese: {近年|きんねん}は{家族葬|かぞくそう}に{対応|たいおう}した{小|ちい}さな{葬儀場|そうぎじょう}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: In recent years, small funeral halls catering to family-only funerals have been increasing.

notes:
A compound of {葬儀|そうぎ} (funeral ceremony) and {場|じょう} (place, hall). This is one of several terms for funeral-related facilities in Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {葬儀場|そうぎじょう}を{予約|よやく}する — to reserve a funeral hall
- {葬儀場|そうぎじょう}に{集|あつ}まる — to gather at the funeral hall
- {葬儀場|そうぎじょう}の{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう} — funeral hall parking lot
- {民間|みんかん}の{葬儀場|そうぎじょう} — private funeral hall

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {斎場|さいじょう} — funeral facility (formal term, often refers to public/municipal facilities; can include crematoriums)
- {葬儀会館|そうぎかいかん} — funeral ceremony hall (often the marketing name used by funeral companies)
- {告別式場|こくべつしきじょう} — farewell ceremony venue (specifically for the farewell portion of the funeral)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Most Japanese funerals today are held at dedicated {葬儀場|そうぎじょう} rather than at home or at temples. The typical sequence involves an {通夜|つや} (wake) on the evening before, followed by the {告別式|こくべつしき} (farewell ceremony) the next day, and then {火葬|かそう} (cremation) at a {火葬場|かそうば}.
